nodes.name: Building a string in one pass
nodes.description: Scan once and append to a result (or rewrite in place with read/write indices) instead of repeated insertion or concatenation.

facets.implement: Appends with += or push_back, reverses once at the end when needed, and handles separators exactly.
facets.trace: Can show the result after each word or character.
facets.adapt: Adapts the same scan to reversing words, keeping a prefix or trimming spaces.

misconceptions.desc: Left leading, trailing or repeated spaces when splitting or joining words.
Reversed the whole string but not each word back (or the reverse).
Inserted at the front of the result repeatedly (O(n²)) instead of appending and reversing once.
Walked the index past the end while skipping spaces.

nodes.name: Depth counter for parentheses
nodes.description: Track open-minus-close depth while scanning; depth alone tells nesting and where each balanced part starts and ends, no stack needed.

facets.recognize: Sees that only the count of open brackets matters, so a counter replaces a stack.
facets.implement: Updates the depth and decides what to keep in the right order.
facets.trace: Can show the depth after each character.

misconceptions.desc: Changed the depth before deciding whether to keep the character (or after), so outer parentheses were kept or inner ones dropped.
Pushed characters on a stack when only the depth count matters.
Read the maximum depth before incrementing it (or after decrementing).

nodes.name: Character mapping in both directions
nodes.description: Keep a mapping from characters of s to t and from t to s; both must stay consistent at every position.

facets.recognize: Sees that a one-to-one correspondence needs a check in both directions.
facets.implement: Maintains two maps (or two arrays of last positions) and checks both at each index.

misconceptions.desc: Checked only s -> t, so two characters of s could map to the same character of t.
Compared character counts, which ignores positions.

nodes.name: Expand around center
nodes.description: Every palindrome has a center; expand from each of the 2n - 1 centers (odd and even length) while the two ends match.

facets.recognize: Uses center expansion for longest palindromic substring and counting palindromic substrings.
facets.explain: Explains why there are 2n - 1 centers and why expansion gives O(n²) instead of O(n³).
facets.implement: Expands with bounds checks and recovers start and length correctly when expansion stops.
facets.trace: Can show l and r during an expansion.

misconceptions.desc: Expanded only around single characters, missing even-length palindromes.
Read s[l - 1] or s[r + 1] without checking bounds while expanding.
Computed the palindrome's start or length wrongly after expansion stopped (length is r - l - 1).
Checked every substring for being a palindrome (O(n³)).

nodes.name: Parsing numbers and symbols from text
nodes.description: Read text character by character: skip whitespace, read a sign, accumulate digits and clamp before overflow; map symbols through a lookup table.

facets.implement: Handles whitespace, sign, digits and the first invalid character in order, checking overflow before it happens.
facets.adapt: Converts in both directions (Roman to integer and back) with a greedy table that includes subtractive pairs.

misconceptions.desc: Checked for overflow after the multiply-add instead of before, or accumulated in int.
Handled whitespace, sign and digits in the wrong order (accepted a sign after digits, or spaces after the sign).
Did not stop at the first non-digit character.
Missed the subtractive rule: a smaller numeral before a larger one is subtracted (IV, IX, XL).
For integer to Roman, left the subtractive values (900, 400, 90, 40, 9, 4) out of the greedy table.

nodes.name: Sliding window
nodes.description: Keep a window [l, r] that satisfies a condition: extend r, shrink l while the condition breaks. Count 'exactly k' as atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1).

facets.recognize: Spots longest/shortest/count of subarrays or substrings under a condition that stays valid as the window shrinks.
facets.explain: Explains why each index enters and leaves the window once (O(n)).
facets.implement: Shrinks with a while loop, updates counts on both edges and counts r - l + 1 windows ending at r.
facets.adapt: Turns 'exactly k' into a difference of two 'at most' counts.

misconceptions.desc: Shrank the window with if instead of while, leaving it invalid.
Counted windows wrongly (the number of substrings ending at r is r - l + 1).
Tried to count 'exactly k' directly instead of atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1).
Did not decrement or erase counts when the left edge moved, so the distinct count went stale.
Enumerated all substrings (O(n²) or worse) where a window works.

nodes.name: Enumerating substrings with running state
nodes.description: For each start, extend the end one character at a time and update the state (counts, max, min) instead of recomputing it.

facets.recognize: Sees when O(n²) substrings are acceptable and state can be carried as the end moves.
facets.implement: Resets state when the start moves and updates it incrementally as the end moves.

misconceptions.desc: Recomputed counts for every substring from scratch (O(n³)).
Did not reset the counts when the start index moved.
